It's strongly implied that it was Jack's obsession with his work, more than anything, that led to their breakup. Cain and Abel: The Abel to Marie's Cain. Demoted to Extra: After appearing prominently in season 2, she makes one brief appearance in the 3rd season and is never seen again.

characters.name: Bob Warner
characters.description: Kate and Marie's father, a businessman whose assets are supposedly being used to fund terrorists. Red Herring: His (would-be) son-in-law suspects him, but neither of them knows that his daughter Marie is responsible.

characters.name: Reza Naiyeer
characters.description: The fiance of Marie Warner. Character Death: Reza is murdered by his own fiance. He Knows Too Much: He finds out who moved the funds just as Marie bursts in, killing the agent with him. He then gets killed shortly afterward. Red Herring: He and his would-be father-in-law were this. Was It All a Lie?: His last words.

characters.name: Carla Matheson
characters.description: Domestic Abuse: On the receiving end. Killed Offscreen: Gary killed her and stuffed her in the trunk of his car. What the Hell, Hero?: She calls Kim out for trying to take Megan the first time... in spite of being the one to tell her to take Megan and scram before her father did something in the first place, thanks to Gary's abuse leaving her in an unstable frame of mind.

characters.name: Megan Matheson
characters.description: Put on a Bus: With her aunt.

characters.name: Yusuf Auda
characters.description: An intelligence agent from a Middle Eastern country during Day 2. Nice Guy: Once they get over the distrust, Jack and him work perfectly together. Character Death: He's beaten to death by racists. Made of Iron: He grabbed to life long enough to tell Jack about what happened.

characters.name: Alex Hewitt
characters.description: The computer hacker who created the Cyprus recording. He’s highly nervous. Character Death: Fell and hit his head on a protruding pipe. Spanner in the Works: Knowledge of his involvement in the terrorist plot is what draws Peter Kingsley out into the open.

characters.name: Julia Milliken
characters.description: The wife of Alan Milliken, one of President David Palmer's most important and influential backers. Character Death: Julia kills herself rather than go to jail. Despair Event Horizon: Sherry leaving her to take the full rap for her husband's death drives her over the edge, as does Wayne's minimal communication with her shortly thereafter. Unfortunate in the latter case, in that Wayne was avoiding conversation because he was too busy attempting to confront Sherry at the time. Driven to Suicide: After killing Sherry, Julia shoots herself. Jerkass Woobie: While she is a Social climber and a trophy wife, she did not want Alan to die, and ends up confessing (first to Wayne, then to the police) her part. All and all, she ends up wrecked with guilt, fear, and feeling completely alone. No wonder she despairs and kills Sherry, and then kills herself.

characters.name: Bruce Foxton
characters.description: A private investigator who assisted Wayne Palmer in breaking into Sherry Palmer's home to look for the medicine prescription bottle that would incriminate her in the death of Alan Milliken during Day 3. Determinator: He refuses to leave until they recover the bottle of medicines. Odd Friendship: With Wayne Palmer. He honestly seems to like and trust him. Sociopathic Hero: He is so nonchalant about some of his criminals actions it becomes hilarious. Not that Sherry did not have that punch coming.

characters.name: Paul Raines
characters.description: Audrey's ex-husband, a British businessman. He is at first accused of helping the terrorist Marwan but he becomes Jack's ally. Amicable Exes: When he finally accepts their marriage is over and Audrey is moving on with Jack, Paul is upset but handles it graciously and comes to support them and wants Audrey to be happy. Butt-Monkey: Tortured by the man his wife left him for, discovers he is Marwan'sUnwitting Pawn, tortured again by the bad guys, gets shot and paralyzed andfinally diesbecause Jack forces the medical staff to save a man with critical info instead of him. Death of the Hypotenuse: Subverted; his death ends the love triangle involving him, Audrey, and Jack, but doesn't happen until after Audrey had by all indications decided to break things off with Jack and give her marriage with Paul another go, meaning thatJackwas technically the hypotenuse. Fire-Forged Friends: Briefly becomes this with Jack. They start off antagonistic (mostly on his end, as he's still registering the notion that his wife is moving on with someone else in her life), but they develop a bond as they attempt to retrieve Marwan's files and are forced to fight back against theMc Lennen-Forster mercenaries.

characters.name: Debbie Pendleton
characters.description: Behrooz's girlfriend. Character Death: She's poisoned by Dina Araz. Locked Out of the Loop: Behrooz's parents disapprove of his relationship with Debbie because they worry about her breaking this. When they fear that she witnessed something critical to their plans, they have her killed before Behrooz can move her to safety. Maligned Mixed Relationship: With Behrooz. Sacrificial Lamb: Her death serves two purposes. The first is to show that Behrooz's parents aren't screwing around. The second is for her death to cement Behrooz's decision in not wanting aid Marwan's cause.

characters.name: Andrew Paige
characters.description: An old classmate of Chloe O'Brian and computer programmer working in Los Angeles during Day 4. All for Nothing: Andrew's tip never gets noticed because everybody was distracted by Secretary Heller's kidnapping. Marwan is able to control California's nuclear power plants and force some of them to meltdown, killing thousands. Butt-Monkey: Things do not fare well for this guy. His coworkers are all killed, his mother is murdered as well, he spends a whole episode being held hostage by Kalil Hasan before his associates beat him half to death, and Jack barely saves him in time, but even then he's last seen in critical condition. Worse, the reason Jack let him remain a hostage, to trail Hasan back to where Audrey and her father were being held, ended up being pointless as Hasan realized he was being followed and killed himself, so Jack let Andrew remain prisoner and almost let him die all for nothing. She Knows Too Much: Andrew calls Chloe after discovering the terrorists placing nodes which would allow them to control internet traffic. For this, his mother and co-workers and he is abducted.

characters.name: Barry Landes
characters.description: The older, psychiatrist boyfriend of Kim. Jerkass: He's a condescending asshole to Jack every time he speaks. May–December Romance: He's much older than Kim.

characters.name: Diane Huxley
characters.description: Jack's girlfriend at the beginning of Day 5. Mama Bear: For her son. Satellite Love Interest: Her only purpose is to show Jack's attempt to start a new life after faking his death. After he returns to CTU, she exits the plot with little fanfare.

characters.name: Derek Huxley
characters.description: The teenage son of Diane Huxley. It's All About Me: He's mostly concerned with how Diane dating Jack affects him. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Sure, he's an enormous prick but he does love his mother and is only really guilty of being a teenage dickhead. The Load: Derek only seems capable of being a detriment to everyone around him. Most notably, he tries to rush in and warn Jack about the attack on the airport, only to end up being captured by the terrorists himself, accomplishing nothing other than giving Jack another hostage to rescue and being threatened to force Jack to do the terrorists' bidding. Mama's Boy: He's very close to his mother, and resents Jack for dating her.

characters.name: Walid Al-Rezani
characters.description: The regional director of the Islamic-American Alliance, an advocacy group for Muslims living in the United States, during Day 6. The Mole: For the FBI, within the detention centre.

characters.name: Ray Wallace
characters.description: Neighbor of Ahmed Amar, who eventually is forced to a make a deliver in his place when his family is held hostage. Big "NO!": His last words. Butt-Monkey: Spends most of his screen time getting pushed and ordered around by terrorists against his will just to protect his family. And then he finds himself at ground zero of a nuclear explosion. Character Death: He's killed when the nuclear bomb detonates. No Good Deed Goes Unpunished: Ray helps his seemingly harmless neighbor Ahmed, understanding that not everyone with a vaguely Middle-Eastern name is a terrorist. Unfortunately, Ahmedisa terrorist who takes his entire family hostage and forces Ray to carry out acts of terrorism for him, ultimately culminating in Ray's death.

characters.name: Hamri Al-Assad
characters.description: Assad is a well-known terrorist with a history of hate of the West spanning 20 years but by Day 6, he has decided to renounce violence and open negotiations. Good Is Not Nice: Assad'sHeel–Face Turndid not diminish his ruthlessness. Guile Hero: For a definition of hero, but Assad is clever, experienced, and very observant. Hero with Bad Publicity: Assad dies saving Wayne Palmer from a bomb but he is blamed for it rather than risk the administration getting humiliated by the fact that this was plotted from within. His people will see him as a great hero who pretended to surrender to the West as part of his plan to assassinate the President. Heel–Face Turn: In an attempt to achieve peace.

characters.name: Carl Benton
characters.description: An ex-special forces friend of Jack. The Atoner: For torturing an innocent civilian to death due to bad intel. Heroic Sacrifice: Carl steps off a landmine when Dubaku gets near, killing himself in the process. Retired Badass: He's given up his life in the Special Forces to take care of children in Sangala. Taking You with Me: He attempts to do this with Dubaku, but Dubaku survives.

characters.name: Ule Matobo
characters.description: The former prime minister of the African nation Sangala who helps Jack to find Dubaku.

characters.name: Marika Donoso
characters.description: Dubaku's innocent girlfriend who is unaware of his true identity. Broken Masquerade: Learns the true nature of her boyfriend, "Samuel Aboa," from Jack and Renee. Car Chase: is in one as Dubaku attempts to flee the country. Heroic Sacrifice: when the FBI lose the trail of herself and Dubaku, she grabs the driver's steering wheel and engineers the crash. She has to unbuckle her seatbelt and lean over the front seat to do this, implying she has accepted that her odds of survival are slim.Which they are. The Infiltration: One of a number of civilians Jack convinces to help him apprehend the villains.

characters.name: Samantha Roth
characters.description: The girlfriend of Roger Taylor. Character Death: She's killed by Brian Gedge. She Knows Too Much: Is aware that Roger was beginning to discover theGovernment Conspiracywithin his mother's administration, and — like him — was killed for that knowledge.

characters.name: Jibraan Al-Zarian
characters.description: An innocent man who has the poor luck to be a Muslim, getting him swept up into Tony Almeida's plans. Action Survivor: When put in a dangerous situation, he shows nerve, creativity under pressure, and an impressive penchant for acting. Dark and Troubled Past: A Pakistani national, his parents were slain in a bombing when he was 11. Fall Guy: Positioned deliberately by Tony. Frame-Up: In addition to his past, which is typical of radicalized extremists, Tony and Cara Bowden manufacture a great deal of false narrative, including bank transfers, to implicate him.

characters.name: Bill Prady
characters.description: The parole officer for Kevin Wade. Character Death: He's murdered by Dana Walsh. Determinator: Very little gets in his way, and it's his determination that leads to Dana deciding to kill him. Hero Antagonist: Prady is just doing his job, he just has the misfortune of tangling with Dana. Horrible Judge of Character: Played with; he immediately works out how untrustworthy Dana is, but the entire reason he comes into contact with her is because he believes that Kevin is a reformed character who's been led astray by Nick. From what we see of them, while Nick is clearly the worse of the two in every regard, Kevin is no saint, and in all likelihood never was.

characters.name: Belcheck
characters.description: A member of the Serbian mob who assisted Jack Bauer's personal mission to stop the assassination of President James Heller during Day 9. Friendly Sniper: Belcheck is a very efficient and deadly sniper, but also a loyal, trustworthy friend. I Owe You My Life: It's implied that Belcheck's loyalty to Jack is because Jack saved Belcheck's life at one point.Chloe O'Brian:I owe Jack; I wouldn't be alive if it weren't for him.Belcheck:Then we have that in common. Only One Name: In his own words:Heller:So what's your name?Belcheck:Belcheck.Heller:'Belcheck' what?Belcheck:Just one word. Like Madonna. Private Military Contractors: Recruited by Jack when he was hiding in mainland Europe.

characters.name: Sherry Palmer
characters.description: The wife of David Palmer until their divorce. She had two children, Keith Palmer and Nicole Palmer. Her brother-in-law was Wayne Palmer and she had a sister-in-law, Sandra Palmer. Ambition Is Evil: Sherry is motivated almost entirely by her utterly vicious, relentless quest for political power. Arch-Enemy: To her own husband, David. Bait the Dog: At the beginning of her appearance in Season 3, Sherry seems calmer and even nicer. She even seems slightly heroic while facing against Alan Milliken... and then she kills him, going further than ever in his evil, and leaving no doubt of what kind of person she truly is. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: While initially she appears as David Palmer's devoted wife, she's actually a political animal willing to do whatever it takes to further her own goals through blackmail, intimidation and outright murder.

characters.name: Nina Myers
characters.description: A distinguished agent at CTU Los Angeles, who was nevertheless a deep-cover mole with connections to Victor Drazen during Day 1. She covertly sold government information to several buyers. She was multilingual and conversant in English, Serbian, German, and Arabic. During Day 1, she was put to work by the Drazens and subsequently exposed as a mole and traitor. She killed several people while attempting to keep her cover and escape, including Jamey Farrell and Teri Bauer. However, she was captured and arrested at the close of the day. During Day 2, she remained in custody but was granted a presidential pardon for giving up the location of her contact Mamud Rasheed Faheen. Later, while questioning Faheen, Nina acquired whereabouts of Syed Ali. She was granted immunity in advance for the murder of Jack Bauer and for Ali's location; however, after giving up his location, she was wounded and apprehended before she could kill him. President Palmer decided to honor the original agreement and she was released afterwards to exiled immunity in North Africa. On Day 3, after attempting to buy the Cordilla virus on behalf of an unidentified client, she was captured by CTU. Though she tricked Jack into activating a hidden worm in CTU's systems, Nina's plan was stopped by Chloe O'Brian. She later attempted to escape, but Kim found her and Jack eventually shot her, and when she was wounded Jack stood over her, sent Kim out of the room and determined she did not have any information that could help them—with that he finally took his revenge and fatally shot her. Arch-Enemy: The first of Jack Bauer's three most hated nemeses throughout the show, followed by bothCharlesLoganandCheng Zhi. Of the three, she's the earliest killed and her impact on the show is the most contained to Jack's enmity with her, as she always appears as a hired Mook for the season'sBig Badwhile never reaching that status herself.

characters.name: Mandy
characters.description: A professional assassin for hire who participated in two conspiracies to assassinate President David Palmer (Days 1 and 2) and assisted Habib Marwan during Day 4. The name, Mandy, was the alias that she most frequently used. Over the years, Mandy proved to be a formidable adversary to the agents of CTU Los Angeles. She seemed to have spent most of her time completely under the radar, surfacing only to cause havoc at a critical moment, then vanishing into obscurity once more. She alternately collaborated with an international oil consortium and fundamentalist Islamic terror cells, apparently loyal to none but herself. On Day 4, Mandy was finally apprehended by CTU for her role in helping Habib Marwan kidnap Secretary of Defense James Heller. In exchange for her cooperation in stopping Marwan, she was granted a presidential pardon for her many crimes, including the attempted assassination of President David Palmer. Back-to-Back Badasses: In theDeadlinenovel, she briefly fulfills this role with Jack as they dispatch a team of SVR soldiers onboard a train. Closest Thing We Got: In theDeadlinenovel, it turns out that Mandy is the only contact Jack is aware of he can get a lead on at short notice, and the only person in his general vicinity who can help him enact his plan ofFaking the Dead.

characters.name: Jonathan Matijevich (Martin Belkin)
characters.description: An Eastern-European assassin who has had plastic surgery to act as Martin Belkin, a famous photographer who would be attending and shooting photographs at a campaign breakfast with David Palmer on the day of the L.A. Presidential Primary. Matijevich plans to assassinate Palmer instead. Can't Kill You, Still Need You: Jack attempts to shoot him before he can get close to Palmer, but Belkin informs him that doing so would lead Gaines to find out and kill Teri and Kim in retaliation. Famed in Story: According to theHouse Special Subcommittee's Findingstie-in book, he's well-known to authorities in his pre-surgery guise, as he was a suspect in the assassination of a CIA operative based in Munich, as well as a failed 1999 terrorist attack on the Reichstag in Germany. Put on a Bus: The last the audience sees of him, he flees from the breakfast event after Jack successfully gets Palmer out of the room by causing a ruckus. He's never mentioned in the show again and never appears on-screen, though theHouse Special Subcommittee's Findingstie-in book (published after S1) suggests that Matijevich went back into hiding in Eastern Europe in order to evade the authorities. Red Herring: An interesting subversion — Belkin (that is, the photographer) acts as the first such example in the series, with the audience being led to believe that he's a double agent or assassin who's flying to the U.S. to kill Palmer, as the opening montage of the show hints at. It isn't until Mandy manipulates him to get his keycard that he's revealed to be the herring. A single episode later, an assassin who looks like him shows up and takes the role he would have had, with the actual intent of killing Palmer.

characters.name: Carl Webb
characters.description: An associate of David Palmer during his campaign for president during Day 1. He was a member of the senator's staff, but was fired when David learned about a cover-up. Blackmail: Tries this on Palmer over the incident his son was involved in.

characters.name: Gary Matheson
characters.description: The abusive husband of Carla and father of Megan. He was the employer of Kim Bauer, his daughter's au pair, during Day 2. Abusive Parent: To his daughter, who's terrified of him. Ax-Crazy: Kills his own wife, murders a police officer and tries to murder Kim and Megan afterwards before being killed himself. Cop Killer: One of his victims is a police officer. Character Death: Kim shoots and kills him in self-defense.

characters.name: Marcus, Rouse & Cole
characters.description: Three crooks who took Kate hostage and threatened to destroy the Cyprus recording Jack needed to prove that the Middle Eastern government was not behind the nuclear bomb threat. Disproportionate Retribution: Yes Marcus, destroy the one bit of evidence Jack needs and thus doom a lot of innocent lives all because he killed one of your pals in an incident that resulted from you trying to kill an innocent person. Even Evil Has Standards: Cole, who's against Marcus trying to kill Kate and eventually attacks him when he attempts to resist Jack. Hero Killer: They murder one of Jack's allies because he's of Arab descent. Jerkass:EspeciallyMarcus.

characters.name: Alan Milliken
characters.description: One of President David Palmer's earliest and biggest financial supporters, and the chief executive officer of Milliken Enterprises. Asshole Victim: While the circumstances of his death are appalling to everyone except for Sherry in-universe, and ultimately confirm Sherry's place past theMoral Event Horizonafter two and a half seasons of dancing around it, it's still hard to feel bad for this guy. Especially after his efforts to sabotage David's healthcare plan, which would probably hurt a significant portion of Americans, all because of a petty grudge against Wayne. This is even more infuriating because he himself is a very sick individual. But no, no empathy there.Not to mention his implied murder of a guy, because he was going to testify against her for a hit and run he commited.On the other hand, his death is kinda pathetic and pitiful. Not to mention his implied murder of a guy, because he was going to testify against her for a hit and run he commited. On the other hand, his death is kinda pathetic and pitiful. Character Death: Sherry practically talks him to death. Their confrontation is so heated that he dies from a heart attack.

characters.name: Jason Pillar
characters.description: A former FBI agent and Charles Logan's executive assistant during Day 8. Alas, Poor Villain: Just when he gave up and was about to save Jack's life, he is killed by Logan. Combined with his previous scene with Jack, it makes it somewhat pitiful, considering also how pointless it ends being (Jack survives, and Logan ends up with brain damage). Asshole Victim: Logan executes him when their plans are ruined. Somehow subverted. Character Death: He's killed by Logan, seemingly out of sheer frustration. The Dragon: For Charles Logan. He seems to be a fairly loyal number two, and sort of looks up to his boss.

characters.name: Kevin Wade
characters.description: A former acquaintance of Dana Walsh prior to Day 8. Blackmail: How he gets Dana under his thumb, as he previously knew her as 'Jenny'. Character Death: Kevin is killed by his partner-in-douchebaggery Nick. Death Equals Redemption: Downplayed, but he still tries to save Dana and Cole from his partner. Domestic Abuse: He gets physical with Dana more than once.

characters.name: Nick Coughlin
characters.description: Ax-Crazy: Kills his partner and tries to kill Dana and Cole with fairly little provocation. Character Death: Shot by Cole after he tries to kill him. The Sociopath: Shows hardly any emotion yet shows to be much more ruthless than domestic abuser and all aroundJerkass, Kevin Wade. Stupid Evil: All the time, making Wade look smart by comparison.
